sentences.text:
The petitioners vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 seek quashing of FIR No.0110/2021 dated 22.03.2021 registered under Sections 498A/406/ 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at PS.: BHD Nagar, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom in view of the Mediation Settlement dated 30.11.2022 arrived at between the parties.

2. This petition is accompanied by the Settlement dated 30.11.2022 and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
CRL.M.C. 6700/2023 page 1 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-
verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 19/09/2023 at 23:22:06 3.
Petitioner nos.1 to 3 and as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the Investigating Officer.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.
5. Learned APP for the State accepts notice.
He confirms that he has no objection to the quashing of the said FIR.

6. Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce Amit Ahlawat & Ors vs State Through Sho Ps Bhd Nagar & Anr on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159569848/
1 by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 03.08.2023.

sentences.text:
She further affirms the Settlement dated 30.11.2022 whereby the petitioner no.1 and 3 have agreed to pay respondent no.2 a sum of Rs.7,00,000/- out of which a sum of Rs.4,50,000/- has already paid to respondent no.2 and the remaining amount of Rs.2,50,000/- has been handed over to the respondent no. 2 vide DD nos.259072 issued on 14.09.2023 on Axis Bank, Branch: Nazafgarh, New Delhi and vide DD No.394080 issued on 14.09.2023 on Cananra Bank, Micro Finance Branch, Nazafgarh, New Delhi in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present, past and future),
stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

7. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 CRL.M.C. 6700/2023 page 2 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 19/09/2023 at 23:22:06 SCC 466, this Court is of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.

8. Accordingly, the petition is allowed and FIR No.0110/2021 dated 22.03.2021 under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 registered with PS.: BHD Nagar, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom are quashed, subject to the petitioners providing at least 5 first-aid kits to the PS.: BHD Nagar, Delhi within a period of a week from today.
9. This Court is highly appreciative of the gesture of goodwill shown by the petitioners.
10. Accordingly, the present petition alongwith the pending applications, if any, stands disposed of.

11. List the matter for compliance on 09.10.2023 before the Roster Bench.
